newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends up slighty, new highs hit.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends up slighty, new highs hit.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures settled barely firmer after surging to life-of-contract highs across the board earlier.

Steady producer selling capped the rally but prices managed to cling to gains by the close. Benchmark July ended up 0.03 cent at 11.51 cents per lb after trading from a new contract high of 11.58 cents to a day's low of 11.34 cents. October finished up the same at 11.32 cents, while the rest settled 0.06 and 0.04 cent firmer.
Analysts expect prices to march higher as open interest continues to climb. As of early Tuesday, open interest in July was up 2,665 lots at 77,212 lots. October gained 4,276 lots to 56,789 lots.

While the recent buying spree has pushed the market into an overbought situation, leaving analysts to wonder how much more buying the funds can sustain, a pullback is not likely until players begin to roll July positions ahead of the expiry on June 30.
"The rolling out of July could intensify, which would bring about an opportunity for a pullback," a trader said.

The producers are expected to limit gains at each tick higher, while resistance on the charts was pegged at 11.65 to 11.70 cents, a high from late April, for July sugar. Support was seen from 11.20 to 11.00 cents.
An estimated 33,315 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Tuesday's official 37,354 lots.
Honduras said today it produced 5.3 million 100-lb bags (around 240,000 tonnes) of sugar in the current season, representing a 500,000-bag increase over last year.
